topic: A removed namespace whose only residue
canonical_claim: A removed namespace whose only residue is `_files` promotes its cleanup item to `Completed` on the first fold, so the janitor cannot key its reclaim logic off `Pending` state alone.

topic: Non per namespace fold seal capacity
canonical_claim: Non-per-namespace fold-seal capacity terms (`btr` per run segment, `cnd` per gc-shard) are untouched by the removal-ordering decision and do not disappear along with the Σ-index-set capacity argument.

topic: Probe A has two documented blind
canonical_claim: Probe A has two documented blind spots it does not catch: a hole that reproduces identically in both enumerations, and a namespace dropped wholesale from one enumeration (no `ref_tables` entry, so the comparison loop never visits it); widening the witness rule to use the pre-scan's own maximum was considered and rejected because it would permanently block the cursor on a namespace whose logs were legitimately cleaned between the walks.

topic: stale_edge_verdict returns unchecked on any partial
canonical_claim: `stale_edge_verdict` returns `unchecked` on any partial scan, with positive findings still checked first, because a partial scan can only weaken a proof of absence, never invalidate evidence of presence.

topic: The chosen fix Fix 4 for
canonical_claim: The chosen fix (Fix 4) for the deposed-leader stray-Clean defect makes GC freshness metadata add-only: GC never transitions Condemned to Clean on a spare (the spare-side `clearSparedMeta` call and helper are removed); only a writer that has displaced the body with a fresh incarnation token publishes Clean, via `uploadFromSource` + `writeResurrectMetaClean`/`copyForwardFromCondemned`. Accepted cost: a spared hash stays Condemned until a writer resurrects it (write amplification on recurring-hash churn); normal reads never consult the meta so this is safe.; Any future §5 revival must keep spare tombstones uncleared until a writer resurrects the blob with a fresh token.

topic: The hot cold layout split changed
canonical_claim: The hot/cold layout split changed GC discovery to GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/, making discovery proportional to ref shards rather than manifest backlog.

topic: GC runs as a background lease
canonical_claim: GC runs as a background lease-holder loop and its safety does not depend on leadership uniqueness; concurrent or stale leaders may duplicate work but must not mis-delete.; The GC lease is work de-duplication rather than mutual exclusion: one `gc/state` CAS adopts a round, attempt-scoped artifacts isolate leaders, pre-CAS destructive work uses published state, and exact-token deletes protect newer incarnations.

topic: The advisory GC heartbeat is stored
canonical_claim: The advisory GC heartbeat is stored in `gc/hb` as `{owner, hb_seq}` and is advanced independently of round progress to prevent a live slow leader from being falsely stolen.

topic: over-protective baseline rebuild
canonical_claim: A forced GC rebuild over-protects unowned manifests that are not provably build-dead, preferring bounded leaks over violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY` through under-counting. GC baseline rebuild is deliberately over-protective rather than under-protective: a build alive across journal trim has no journal evidence, so its manifests look unowned; the rebuild includes edges for every unowned manifest that is not provably build-dead, over-protecting rather than risking under-count. An unowned manifest that later dies with no journal evidence leaks its blob's edges for one bounded rebuild-to-rebuild window, `fsck`-visible as `unaccounted` — preferred to violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY`.

topic: GC safety is independent of the
canonical_claim: GC safety is independent of the advisory heartbeat; the heartbeat is the minimal addition needed to prevent a slow leader's frozen round sequence from triggering a false steal.

topic: The root local model shows that
canonical_claim: The root-local model shows that a target-sharded fold needs one global coordinator fence and paired old-binding `−1` deltas; per-reducer fencing or inferring the old target from the new ref is unsafe.

topic: The E3 GC redesign used root
canonical_claim: The E3 GC redesign used root-local part manifests and source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, removed the registry, and added a shard-incarnation ABA guard.

topic: The E4 GC and writer settlement
canonical_claim: The E4 GC and writer settlement uses a one-pass heartbeat ack-floor round, writer point-reads of freshness metadata instead of a `RetireView`, retired rows inside the snapshot run, and a ref snapshot plus append log instead of a mutable root-shard manifest.; The GC-side ack-floor one-pass round is current, while the writer-side ack-floor and `RetireView` synchronization was deleted by `55b76af5998`; these are separate mechanisms.; The regular GC round is one pass consisting of a heartbeat ack floor, one `LIST` discovery sweep, a three-cursor fold, pre-CAS deletes, and one `gc/state` CAS. The ack-floor GC redesign replaces O(universe) per-round fence and recheck phases with a merged per-server heartbeat, a current retired list, and a one-pass three-cursor merge. The planned one-pass ack-floor round computes the heartbeat floor before discovery, folds and merges deltas, deletes graduated entries by exact token, writes retired-list objects, and then performs one `gc/state` CAS; `fence` and `recheck` are removed. The ack-floor GC round replaces fence and recheck phases with a three-cursor streaming merge and one `gc/state` CAS; graduation requires `condemn_round < min_ack` and two-phase `delete_pending` handling. The current GC implementation (Gc class, CasGc.h) is a leader-paced ack-floor redesign (spec 2026-07-02): one pass per round consisting of a heartbeat ack floor over MountLease.observed_gc_round, a three-cursor merge fold, two-phase condemn/graduation deletion, and a single gc/state CAS; the older fence_round/recheck terminology survives only as fossil comments/variable names.

topic: retired sentinel rows
canonical_claim: Retired rows are represented as `kCondemned` sentinel rows inside the snapshot run rather than as a separate retired-list object. Retired entries can ride the source-edge snapshot as condemned-sentinel rows, reducing the GC merge from three cursors to two; a separate incremental LSM snapshot is an independent later optimization.

topic: The D1 implementation plan replaces gc
canonical_claim: The D1 implementation plan replaces `gc/registry` discovery with `LIST(cas/refs/)` and reclaims empty ref-shard objects so `dropNamespace` no longer leaks a monotone registry and empty shard objects.; D1 makes `LIST(cas/refs/)` the discovery authority, retains ambiguity detection across pages as a fail-closed condition, and removes `gc/registry`, `RootsRegistry`, `rootsRegistryKey`, `ensureRegistered`, the registry-fence sub-step, and the `_registry` cursor branch.

topic: The D1 design collapses the prior
canonical_claim: The D1 design collapses the prior fence coordinates into two orthogonal coordinates: immutable shard `incarnation` for identity and birth ordering, plus pool-global GC `round` for the writer retire-view floor.

topic: dropNamespace appends an explicit tombstone as
canonical_claim: `dropNamespace` appends an explicit tombstone as the last journal event after ref removals, and GC deletes the shard only when it is empty, tombstoned, and folded past a completed fence using `deleteExact(rootShardKey(ns, shard), token)`.

topic: After registry removal GC fences only
canonical_claim: After registry removal, GC fences only discovered shards from `LIST(cas/refs/)`; an absent shard is not minted or fenced, and create ordering is supplied by the precommit gate.

topic: The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC
canonical_claim: The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC protocol documentation to cover lease/election, rounds, orphan and ref removal, shard reclaim, incarnation, registry removal, attempt-scoped generations, TLA+ references, and S3 budget links.

topic: The current retired list design adds
canonical_claim: The current retired-list design adds `RetiredEntry::condemn_round`, adds `GcState::retired_refs`, uses `cas_gc_state` version 4, rejects v3 fail-closed, and has `RetireView::refresh` GET `gc/state` followed by each referenced retired-list object without LIST.; The retired list is one current sorted candidate set referenced by `gc/state.retired_refs`; per-round retired sets keyed by `retiredKey(...)` and the multi-round `RetireView` fetch protocol are removed.

topic: The redesigned regular GC round targets
canonical_claim: The redesigned regular GC round targets O(delta) plus O(servers) S3 requests; its only universe-proportional operation is the existing LIST sweep, which costs O(universe/1000) LIST requests.; The redesigned steady-state round budget is one LIST sweep plus O(servers) heartbeat GETs, O(D) changed-shard GETs, O(window) manifest GETs, O(gc_shards) run GET/PUTs, candidate HEADs, graduated DELETEs, O(D) coverage PUTs, and one `gc/state` CAS, with no O(universe) GET/PUT phase.

topic: gc state removes fence_version adds current
canonical_claim: `gc/state` removes `fence_version`, adds current retired-list references and checksums, and is updated with one CAS per pass containing the round, generation adoption, retired references, and coverage.

topic: fence_round is no longer bumped every
canonical_claim: `fence_round` is no longer bumped every round; it remains only as the birth floor stamped at root-shard creation for THM-NO-RETURN newborn ordering.

topic: Graduation is two phase a pass
canonical_claim: Graduation is two-phase: a pass marks fresh graduates with `delete_pending = true` and keeps them published, while `deleteExact` runs only for entries already pending in the previous published list.

topic: Snapshot run streaming scope includes T2
canonical_claim: Snapshot-run streaming scope includes T2 streaming reads and T0 reference-parent runs for empty-delta shards; T1 delta-runs are deferred to a subsequent specification.

topic: The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration
canonical_claim: The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration over batches of at most `rebuild_edge_budget` edges, feeding the previous attempt's runs back as `prior_runs`; this provides O(budget) memory without new spill/merge classes.

topic: GC trim uses mutateShard as a
canonical_claim: GC trim uses `mutateShard` as a `WholeShard` queue item, so trim rewrites no longer race writers even though trim still flushes alone.

topic: GC Lever A skips the expensive
canonical_claim: GC Lever A skips the expensive in-degree snapshot rebuild on rounds with no destructive decision; Lever B, an incremental point-updatable in-degree store, remains out of scope.

topic: Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for
canonical_claim: Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for a renewal is conservative for the GC floor because it can only lower `min_ack` and delay graduation; lease expiry is the failure that must be avoided.

topic: The phase 4 GC optimization skips
canonical_claim: The phase-4 GC optimization skips unchanged namespaces so an idle round approaches O(servers) reads and a small-delta round costs O(delta), with a mandatory TLA+ proof that owner-removal events are never skipped.
